newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Hong Kong interbank rates were steady to firmer in quiet trading on Thursday with activities focused on short-dated money, dealers said.
The overnight rate firmed to 4-15/16 7/8 percent from 4-1/2 3/8 and three-month money was steady at 5-5/8 9/16 against 5-5/8 8/16 percent.
Dealers said short-dated money firmed following firmer U.S. rates and underlying rollover demand ahead of the yearend.
"Short-dated money is likely to stay firm due to corporate and technical demand ahead of the yearend," one dealer said.
Trading on government paper largely followed the sharp drops by U.S. Treasuries overnight, dealers said.
One-week bill yields rose to 4.09 percent from 3.89 percent on Wednesday and one-month yielded 4.30 versus 4.19.

Three-year note yields edged up to 6.14 percent from 6.04 percent, the seven-year yield rose to 7.12 from 6.98 percent and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.34 versus 7.19. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6370
